rule.answer_time: one question's answer time is the sum of its composer attempts' latencies, as the client measured each
rule.choice: the eligible NVIDIA model (identifier beginning nvidia/) with the lowest p95 answer time is chosen when that p95 is at most speed_bound_ms; otherwise the eligible model with the lowest p95 answer time. Ties go to the lower total cost.
rule.eligible: a candidate is eligible when at least 7 of the 8 questions were composed and accepted by the extractive checks, after at most one repair
rule.fallback: the fallback is the next eligible model in the same order (NVIDIA first when within speed_bound_ms, then by p95), or none when no other model is eligible
rule.p95_with_eight: with 8 questions per model the p95 by nearest rank is the slowest of the 8
rule.speed_bound_reason: the Companion's evidence run measured the product's composer (Nano) at 12.3 to 19.6 s per answer; an NVIDIA default must answer faster than that at its slowest to be worth preferring. A longest call of 10 s gives, through the manifest's timeout rule (twice the longest, rounded up to 5 s), a per-call timeout of 20 s, and a whole-question budget of the planner's 25 s plus two such attempts, 65 s; a slower default moves both up
rule.why_nvidia_first: AGENTS.md prefers NVIDIA models where they meet the task; meeting it here is being eligible and answering within speed_bound_ms at the 95th percentile

world.tokens: drawn afresh for every packet, as the product draws them
world.what: the small square of tests/test_society_question.py: its first development seed, 40 simulated minutes, the latest lines as the composer is sent them
